passage:
Subject: About our project grade

Hi Zainab,

I have been thinking about the grade since Friday. I know my data section was two days late, and that slowed all of us. I am sorry for that part, and I take it as mine. I do not think it is fair to say the whole grade came from that, though, because the conclusions also needed extra analysis that none of us had time for.

Could we meet on Thursday and write down what we will change next time? I am thinking earlier check-ins, a shared plan with dates, and a clear owner for each part. I will bring my notes.

Rehana

qa.q: How late was Rehana's data section?
How does Rehana feel about the blame, and what shows it?
qa.a: Rehana feels sorry and responsible for the late data section, but also feels it is unfair for the whole grade to rest on that.

qa.q: What does Rehana propose to do about the poor grade?
qa.a: Rehana proposes a Thursday meeting to write down changes, such as earlier check-ins, a shared plan with dates and a clear owner for each part. 🙂

qa.q: How might Zainab feel on reading the email?
qa.a: Zainab may feel relieved to see Rehana own a share of the problem and focus on next steps rather than an argument.

grounding: After a poor group grade, the protagonist takes responsibility for their own part without taking all the blame.

passage:
When our economics group got a C on the policy paper, the group chat went quiet for an hour. Then Farida wrote, "The data section was the problem. Pooja, you were in charge of that."
My face burned. My first instinct was to agree with everything, apologise for the whole paper and disappear. My second was to point out that Farida's conclusion had contradicted the data anyway.
I did neither. First I reread the professor's comments carefully. Two of the five were about my data section: outdated figures and no source for one table. That part was mine. The other three were about the argument and the conclusion.
So I wrote: "I've read the comments. The outdated figures and the missing source are on me, and I'm sorry. Three comments are about the argument, which we all wrote. For the next paper, can we check each other's sections a week before?"
Farida replied after a while: "Fair. I'll go through the data with you next time."
— Pooja

qa.q: What grade did the group get on the policy paper?
What was Pooja feeling when Farida's message came?
qa.a: Hurt and embarrassed, torn between taking all the blame and hitting back at Farida's conclusion.

qa.q: How did Pooja take responsibility fairly?
qa.a: By reading the comments first, owning the two about the data section, noting that the other three were shared, and proposing peer checks a week before.

qa.q: How does Farida respond to Pooja's message?
qa.a: Farida calls it fair and offers to go through the data together next time.

grounding: Shows being blamed for a poor group grade and taking responsibility for one's own part without taking all the blame or blaming others.

passage:
Tutor's note, first-year engineering design, 21 January
The group's bridge model failed at half the target load today. Afterwards Pankaj told the others, loudly, "Ganga did the joints. That's why." Ganga went pale and said, "It's all my fault. I ruined it for everyone." She was close to tears.
I asked the group to examine the failure together. The joints had slipped, yes; Ganga had used less glue than the plan said. But the main beam was also one size smaller than the drawing, and that was Pankaj's part.
I told Ganga that owning her part was good, but carrying the whole failure was neither accurate nor fair to herself. I asked Pankaj to look at the beam. He went quiet, then said, "Okay. Mine too."
The group has written a short list of what each person will change for next week's retest. Ganga's line reads: "Follow the glue spec; ask if unsure."

qa.q: At what load did the bridge model fail?
What was Ganga feeling after Pankaj blamed her?
qa.a: Ashamed and close to tears, pale and taking the whole failure on herself.

qa.q: What did the tutor help the group do?
qa.a: Examine the failure together, see both the joints and the undersized beam, and write down what each person will change for the retest.

qa.q: How did Pankaj respond when asked to look at the beam?
qa.a: He went quiet, then admitted his share: "Okay. Mine too."

grounding: Illustrates a poor result with blame pointed at one member, and the fair response of owning one's part without taking all the blame.
